fact: Le N'Djam Post reports that under the 2026 finance law 3,000 electronic payment terminals have been deployed in the financial agencies (régies financières), and that télépaiement is expected to become general for taxes and duties.
The 2027 budget orientations say tax, customs and Treasury systems are to be integrated with electronic payment solutions.

The Chad finance ministry received 3,000 smart electronic payment terminals on 24 July 2026, supplied by the World Bank under the PATN project, to modernise public revenue collection; no deployment schedule is stated.

fact: Le N'Djam Post says the 2026 budget year brings mandatory e-invoicing and payments made exclusively by bank or mobile, with all State revenue and spending to be recorded in SIGFIP under a zero-cash, zero-paper principle, according to an expert speaking in a personal capacity.
Finance Minister Tahir Nguilin's circular of 1 September 2025 prohibits cash collection of state revenue by taxes, customs and domains agencies, as the state opts for digital payment.
Tchadinfos says digitalisation of public revenue limits fraud and speeds the entry of funds into the State's coffers.
Tchadinfos reports the finance ministry signed conventions on 18 February 2026 with Moov Money, Airtel Money, Konoom and Cashi to allow public revenue to be paid through mobile money platforms.

fact: The Director General of Taxes said that through the E-Tax platform, launched in 2022, anyone can declare and pay taxes online, with banks and mobile operators facilitating electronic payments.

Finance minister Tahir Hamid Nguilin's 3 July 2025 circular says the tax and customs directorates have integrated E-tax and Sydoniaworld with banks and mobile operators so taxpayers can pay online, and orders telepayment platforms into service by 15 July 2025, after which only telepayment is admitted for collecting customs and tax revenue.
The director general of taxes says E-Tax lets taxpayers pay all taxes and duties they owe online, and that the DGI is interconnected with eight banks.

Chad's customs e-payment system, launched 21 February 2024, lets all customs duties and taxes be paid electronically by SYDONIA World tele-payment, bank transfer or mobile money, with an automatic receipt.
The Chad customs directorate (DGDDI) says an e-payment system for secure electronic payment of duties and taxes was launched in 2024.
